entities.summary:
Jayavarman I, also called Protégé of Victory, is considered to be the last ruler of the united Chenla, the predecessor polity of the Khmer Empire. The united Chenla was a powerful medieval state that controlled much of modern-day Cambodia, parts of Vietnam, and the Mekong Delta in southwestern China. This entity matters historically because it marked the beginning of the Khmer Empire's rise to power and had significant cultural and political implications for the region.

Jayavarman I was born into a noble family and rose to power after the death of his father, King Yasovarman II, in 651 CE. He then proceeded to unite the warring factions of the Chenla and expanded the empire's borders through military conquests and strategic alliances.

One of Jayavarman I's most significant achievements was the establishment of the Khmer Empire's capital, Angkor, which would become a center of trade, culture, and learning for centuries to come.

The legacy of Jayavarman I can be seen in the many ancient temples and ruins that dot the Cambodian countryside, including the famous Angkor Wat temple complex, which was built during his reign.

Despite his significant impact on Khmer history, Jayavarman I's life and reign remain somewhat shrouded in mystery, with many details lost to the sands of time.
